## Reading

Loukissas, Chapter 1, _Local Origins_, pp. 13–26. [Session 3](03-taking-data-apart.qmd) reads the same chapter from a different angle.

## Reading summary

For Loukissas, **local** does not mean small or only geographic. Local conditions can be social, institutional, technical, cultural, or historical. They work at different scales. Data can travel, but they are always made and used in particular settings. The local is also not always good; local categories and practices can reproduce exclusion or bias.

## In class

Students build a **Data Setting Checklist**. The checklist asks eight things about a dataset:

- who made it;
- where it was made;
- when it was made;
- why it was made;
- how it was made;
- for whom it was made;
- under which categories it was recorded;
- what is absent from it.

## Output

The Data Setting Checklist. You use it again in [Session 11](11-describe-your-dataset.qmd) on your own dataset.
